quote: For solar panels for your home, we're offering the bill swap program.
stewart_read: Rep launches into program mechanics before running any verify items (homeowner, roof, utility, interest, bill) — classic premature pitch that invites a financial interrogation the setter isn't equipped to win.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged the customer's excitement warranted skipping straight to the offer to keep momentum.
coaching_implication: Run verify + interest_question first even on a hot lead — the pitch lands harder once the bill and interest are anchored, and it avoids the back-end-cost rabbit hole that followed.

quote: Well, what are the back end costs? If there's no front up upfront, what's the back end?
stewart_read: This is a cost/trust objection about the mechanism of the program; rep answers literally instead of flipping to the customer's actual bill pain.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may not have had a bill number yet to flip against, since bill_amount was never asked — the flip requires the anchor that's missing.
coaching_implication: This traces back to the missed bill_amount capture — without a number to anchor against, the rep has nothing to flip the objection with.

quote: I'm I'm asking what those rates are that you would be paying.
stewart_read: Second touch on the same rate question; rep repeats the same unspecific reassurance instead of pivoting to 'let's grab your actual bill so I can show you the real number.'
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could be intentionally deferring specifics to the closer's proposal stage — but no bridge language ('our specialist will build the real numbers off your bill') was used to signal that.
coaching_implication: Explicitly redirect rate questions to bill capture: 'grab your bill so I can show you exactly what changes' — turns the objection into the verify step instead of stalling on repeated slogans.

quote: So that's who you're with, Dominion?
stewart_read: Rep finally gets the utility confirmed but treats it as a checkbox — doesn't use it to pivot into bill collection or interest question immediately after.
coaching_implication: Immediately follow utility confirmation with the bill-amount ask while the customer is still engaged, before he pivots to 'send me a link.'

quote: So can you send me a link to my email so I can do some reading on your company?
stewart_read: This is functionally the same 'send me info first' deflection the schema flags — rep should treat it as a stall, not a simple request.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may see this as low-stakes since it's just a website, not a full proposal, so no pushback was warranted.
coaching_implication: Use the moment to lock a callback time or continue qualifying ('happy to send that — while I've got you, let's grab your bill so I can also get you a real number') rather than closing the call on a bare concession.

quote: Yeah. I'll just send you our website.
stewart_read: Call ends with zero button-up elements — no time, no next step owned by the rep, no text-follow-up promise tied to anything specific.
coaching_implication: Even a soft exit should get an owned next step: 'I'll send the site now, and let's plan a quick call Thursday once you've had a look' — anchors a return point.
